newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Arafat says Europe must play full role in Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Europe must play full role in Mideast.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Monday it was vital for Europe to play a political role in supporting the Middle East peace process, thus complementing the diplomatic efforts of the United States.
Arafat, speaking after talks with the Dutch presidency of the European Union, noted that the EU was the biggest provider of development aid to the Palestinians.
But he said it was a geopolitical necessity for Europe to play a political role in the region, not just an economic one.
"Our relations with Europe are very important. Peace in the Middle East is very important for Europe. This is a matter of geopolitics. Nobody can avoid it," he told a news conference.
"I am not looking only for the economic card of Europe. The political card of Europe is more important than the economic card," he said.
Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said Europe was keen to play a complementary role alongside Washington in supporting the peace process.
"What we should avoid is a division of roles: the Americans behind the Israelis and Europe behind the Palestinians. That doesn't work. We should avoid that," he said.
The Dutch foreign minister and Prime Minister Wim Kok held two hours of talks with Arafat on Monday morning.
Van Mierlo said politics and economics were so deeply intertwined in the Middle East that they could not be separated.
"It is absolute nonsense to make a distinction between economic roles and political roles. Go to Gaza and you see that every economic thing is a political issue," he said.
Earlier Israeli and U.S. reservations about a diplomatic role for Europe in the Middle East now seemed to have vanished, he added.
Arafat said that without the mediation of both sides, the recent agreement on Israel's withdrawal from Hebron could not have been reached.
"Without the effort done by Europe and America it would have been very difficult for us to achieve the breakthrough of the Hebron agreement," he said.

Arafat met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at Davos in Switzerland on Sunday and is due to meet him again on Thursday to discuss implementation of outstanding points from the Hebron agreement.
